assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: The nine-month 2026 actual is the anchor, not a forecast: revenue of Rp7,639bn in the nine months to September against Rp9,947bn for the whole of FY2025 [S0] leaves FY2026E at about Rp10,250bn once a fourth quarter in line with the witnessed FY2025 quarter (Rp2,611bn, S0) is added, i.e. +3.0 per cent on the year. That is slower than FY2025's +7.2 per cent (S7) because the feed price rises that drove 2025 have not repeated, and the state has brokered a delay in poultry feed price rises to protect farmers (S10). Growth then returns to the volume the market can absorb: national shrimp production was 844,140 tonnes in 2024 and exports were 218,870 tonnes in 2025, broadly flat on the prior year (S9, S3), against an RPJMN target of 1.69m tonnes by 2029 (S9) that is a plan, not a witnessed trend. We carry mid-single-digit growth, tapering to the house macro deck's long-run path, and put the RPJMN stretch case in the bull scenario.

assumptions.label: Gross margin
assumptions.basis: Three witnesses, no free parameters. FY2026E is the nine-month actual: revenue of Rp7,639bn less cost of revenue of Rp6,232bn gives 18.4 per cent [S0], and the fourth quarter is carried at the same rate because nothing in the record says the fourth quarter of a harvest year is better than the first nine months - the witnessed quarters run 18.6, 19.0 and 17.7 per cent, so the full-year figure is the run-rate, not an inflection [S0]. FY2027E carries 19.5 per cent and FY2028E the FY2025 actual of 20.07 per cent (gross profit Rp1,990bn on revenue Rp9,947bn, S7): the 2026 dip is the pass-through lag on an input spike, and the lag closes because the deck's corn and soymeal curves are flat from FY2026E to FY2027E - the level stops rising, so pricing catches up. The recovery pace is the one the company has delivered: 18.7 per cent in FY2023 to 19.9 in FY2024 to 20.1 in FY2025 [S0]. Holding the last actual from FY2028E is not a heroic fade-in: FY2022, FY2024 and FY2025 all printed 19.9-20.1 per cent, through a corn range of US$167-273/t and soymeal of US$321-488/t [S0]. No permanent absorption of input inflation is modelled, because none is witnessed.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025A operating expenses of Rp1,132bn on revenue of Rp9,947bn, 11.4 per cent, after a rise of only 0.7 per cent while revenue grew 7.2 per cent (S7, S0). The nine-month 2026 actual is running higher: revenue of Rp7,639bn less cost of revenue of Rp6,232bn and EBIT of Rp514bn implies opex of about Rp893bn, 11.7 per cent of sales [S0], so the cost base is not levering as fast as the 2025 print suggested. FY2026E is carried at the nine-month rate and drifts down only slowly to 11.2 per cent by FY2030E; no source supports a step improvement, so the witnessed level is carried rather than assumed away.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Carried at the witnessed charge, not restated, after the QC review of round one. The pack reports Rp57.9bn on revenue of Rp9,947bn, 0.6 per cent, which is 1.6 per cent of net fixed assets and low for a feed and processing asset base; the earlier draft lifted it to 2.75 per cent on the argument that the pack's cash-flow arithmetic required it. That argument does not survive the statement the pack does publish: the total of every add-back between net profit and operating cash flow, before working capital, is Rp160bn, Rp376bn and Rp272bn in FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025 and Rp117bn across the nine months to September 2026, and a charge of Rp280bn a year alone sits above the nine-month total [S0]. The residual is also the wrong shape to be depreciation: it swings by a factor of two and a half between years, it is not in the accounts as a separate line, and part of it is working capital the pack's net-working-capital definition leaves out (other current assets and liabilities). No filed cash-flow statement is obtainable through the channels open to us - the company's publications pages are script-rendered and the document system behind them is login-gated - so we cannot witness a different charge, and we do not carry an uplift on an argument alone. The economic case for the uplift is also weaker than it looked: an asset base that wears out at 2.75 per cent of sales must be replaced at roughly that rate to stand still, so most of the add-back the uplift created would have been consumed by the higher capex a coherent steady state needs. Carrying the pack understates the add-back and overstates nothing else; the direction of the error therefore runs in favour of the value case, and section six states the gap.

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025A capex of Rp228bn was 2.3 per cent of revenue, against Rp204bn (2.2 per cent) in FY2024 and Rp117bn (1.3 per cent) in FY2023 [S0]. The company has no announced project cycle and its publications pages do not disclose a forward plan, so the witnessed three-year average of about 2.3 per cent is carried through the forecast and into the terminal year, with no step. The earlier draft stepped capex up to a restated depreciation rate from FY2030E; that restatement is withdrawn, and with the pack's reported charge the witnessed capex is several times depreciation in every year, so the asset base is being renewed rather than consumed and no catch-up step is warranted. The group's capacity build (feed mills at Cikampek, Surabaya, Sidoarjo, Medan and Lampung, S4) is already in the asset base.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: The witnessed September level, held, with no unwind assumed. Working capital was Rp2,194bn on trailing revenue of Rp10,250bn at 30 September 2026, 21.4 per cent [S0], up from Rp1,730bn and 17.4 per cent at the FY2025 year end and from 15.0, 16.3 and 15.1 per cent in the three years before that [S0]; inventory is Rp1,886bn and receivables Rp992bn at the last year end. The previous draft carried 19 per cent between the year end and the quarter, which required a Rp246bn release inside the fourth quarter; the data pack has no 2025 third quarter to establish seasonality and no source shows a fourth-quarter unwind, so the base case carries the level and lets the release be upside. At 21.4 per cent the FY2026E change in working capital is about the full-year absorption the balance sheet has already suffered, and it is the single largest drag on free cash flow. The bull case assumes a two-point release, the bear a two-point further build.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: Effective rates of 32.4 per cent in FY2025, 28.7 per cent in FY2024 and 23.1 per cent in FY2023 [S0] average in the high twenties, above the 22 per cent statutory rate because of non-deductible items and losses in subsidiaries. Carried at 29 per cent, the middle of the witnessed range, rather than at a statutory rate the company has never paid.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: FY2025A interest expense of Rp150bn on opening debt of Rp1,717bn, 8.7 per cent [S0]; the group has repaid its dollar tranche and refinanced into rupiah, so the witnessed cost is carried rather than a lower rate assumed on refinancing.

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: FY2025A interest income of Rp2.0bn on opening cash of Rp99bn is 2.0 per cent [S0]; carried at the witnessed rate, immaterial to the valuation.

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: Debt fell from Rp2,154bn in FY2023 to Rp1,717bn in FY2024 and Rp1,687bn in FY2025 as the company repaid its tranche A facility early [S0]; we assume no new borrowing and no further repayment, the neutral path between the two witnessed directions.

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: Carried, not zeroed. The plug between EBIT and pre-tax profit has been a charge in every year the pack covers: Rp129.6bn in FY2022, Rp37.3bn in FY2023, Rp188.1bn in FY2024 and Rp88.8bn in FY2025 [S0], which is 12.4 per cent of FY2026E EBIT at the last rate. It is a repeating, if unsourced, item (FX and other non-operating charges), and a thesis that turns on earnings recovery cannot carry it at zero while claiming the earnings are real. The last actual is carried flat, the neutral choice against a four-year average of Rp111bn; the bear case adds a further fifth of the charge, and the sensitivity of the value to it is shown in section 5.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: Minority interests are Rp2.7bn of a Rp3,788bn equity base and took Rp0.4bn of FY2025 profit [S0]; carried at the witnessed 0.1 per cent.

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: No dividend is paid: the pack records only a Rp0.3bn residual distribution in FY2025 and a DPS history of zero [S0], and the equity is being rebuilt after the group's earlier losses. Zero is the witnessed policy, not a conservative assumption, and the bull case does not assume a distribution either - the value case rests on the cash being retained or applied to debt.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: Shares outstanding of 59,572m have been unchanged through the pack's history and no rights issue or placement is announced [S0]; carried flat.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: House terminal growth for the rupiah, below the macro deck's long-run Indonesian nominal expansion, and justified by a feed market that grows with aquaculture volumes: national shrimp output has been flat near 844,000 tonnes while the plan targets 1.69m tonnes by 2029 (S9). The terminal rate is the volume plus price path the market has actually delivered, not the plan.

challenges.challenge: The multiple-survival test is run on the wrong entry and reports the opposite of its result. Section 4 calls Rp6,141.3bn "the entry enterprise value"; that is the DCF's own EV (74.11 x 59.572 + 1,723.7 + 3.0). What a buyer pays today is market cap 1,906.3 + debt 1,773.9 - cash 50.3 + minorities 3.0 = Rp3,633.0bn, i.e. 3.6x FY2026E EBITDA. The DCF EV is 6.1x and the terminal value of Rp8,372.1bn implies 5.9x FY2035 EBITDA (8.5x EBIT) - a 64% re-rating. Holding the exit at today's 3.6x cuts TV to Rp5,118bn, the DCF to about Rp55 and the pre-scenario blend to about Rp43, so the 12-month target is about Rp50 (+56%), not Rp63 (+98%). The sentence "we are not asking a future buyer to pay more per unit of earnings than the present one" is false, and the card says implied exit above entry must be argued, not denied.
challenges.answer: Multiple-survival test rerun against the market entry (capitalisation plus net debt) and on the exit multiple itself: about one and a half times the entry on both EV/EBITDA and EV/EBIT, and above the cross-check blend, stated as multiple expansion rather than defended; the exit-at-entry case is described (target falls to roughly the midpoint between the two DCFs, rating survives on the zero-TV DCF of Rp35 against Rp32), and weights moved to 55% perpetuity and 20% zero-TV DCF [S0].

challenges.challenge: Four load-bearing inputs have no source and are jointly fitted to one observation. link1_share 0.10, link2_share 0.22, link1_pass 0.80 and link2_pass 0.80 are all key_input: true and fund record calls them "an ordered estimate" because the annual report is unobtainable. They are tuned to reproduce a single number, the 9M2026 gross margin of 18.4%, so four free parameters against one target is not identification - yet section 3 offers the fit as "the evidence that the pass-through parameters are right". The same four then set FY2026E 18.7% and the fade to 17.4% by FY2035, which is the margin path the DCF capitalises.
challenges.answer: Both cost links removed (link1 and link2 empty in params), which deletes the four unidentified key_inputs; gross margin is now one sourced number per year from the 9M2026 actual to the FY2025 actual at the FY2023-FY2025 pace, with the deck curves disclosed in section 2 and the identification argument written out [S0][S7].

challenges.challenge: The BLOCK flag was cleared with a justification that describes a model the report does not contain. qc_justifications.extreme_call says the links "recover the FY2025 gross margin of 20.1 per cent after the 2026 squeeze, which lifts EBIT from the nine-month run-rate toward the FY2025 level". The model has 18.7% in FY2026E (never 20.1%), EBIT margin 7.0% against FY2025's 8.7%, and 6.2% by FY2035 - EBIT never returns to the nine-month run-rate and moves away from FY2025.
challenges.answer: qc_justifications.extreme_call rewritten to the model actual path: 18.4% at FY2026E rising to the FY2025 actual of 20.07% by FY2028E, EBIT margin 6.7% to 8.7%, D&A at 2.75% of sales, NWC at 21.4% held, WACC of 12.0% inside the band, and two DCFs of which one has no terminal value [S0][S7].

challenges.challenge: Both cross-checks are admittedly defective and still carry 50% of the weight, so the error the report identifies stays in the target. The P/E applies 6.08x to LTM net profit of Rp275.2bn and the EV/EBITDA applies 5.34x to LTM EBITDA of Rp744.1bn, which contains the same Rp57.9bn depreciation the DCF rejects; restating D&A puts that metric at Rp964bn and the method at about Rp57/share instead of Rp38, and FY2026E earnings of Rp407.9bn put the P/E at about Rp42 instead of Rp28. On corrected metrics v0 is about Rp61 and the 12-month target about Rp71, not Rp53/Rp63. Calling the cross-checks "a floor" while giving them half the weight is not a floor.
challenges.answer: Weight on the two multiples cut to 25% combined and 75% to the two DCFs; the report now states the cross-checks are trough-on-trough and treats them as a floor; the restated-D&A metric cannot be fed to the multiple methods because they read the pack LTM, so the weight moved instead [S0].

challenges.challenge: FY2026E needs a fourth-quarter inflection that no source supports. FY gross margin of 18.7% against 9M's 18.4% requires Q4 gross margin of about 19.5% after 18.6% (Q1), 19.0% (Q2) and 17.7% (Q3); FY EBIT of Rp717.2bn against 9M Rp514.3bn requires Q4 EBIT of Rp202.9bn (7.8% margin) against Q3's Rp142.9bn (5.5%); FY net profit of Rp407.9bn against LTM Rp275.2bn requires Q4 net profit of Rp132.7bn against Q4-2025's Rp-3.1bn. Revenue is anchored on the 9M actual; margin and profit are not.
challenges.answer: FY2026E now equals the 9M2026 gross margin of 18.4% and the 9M EBIT run-rate of 6.7%; section 3 states the nine-month-to-year bridge explicitly, with the fourth quarter carried at the FY2025 fourth-quarter revenue and the nine-month margin, so no fourth-quarter inflection is required [S0].

challenges.challenge: The working-capital assumption needs a Rp246bn release in one quarter. FY2026E NWC is 19% x Rp10,250.5bn = Rp1,947.6bn, but NWC was Rp2,193.6bn at 30-Sep-2026 and rose through the year (1,925 / 1,900 / 2,194), so the model requires NWC to fall Rp246bn in Q4. Held flat, FY2026E FCFF drops from Rp338.2bn to about Rp92bn - roughly the whole first-year cash flow. The report asserts as fact that working capital "will release as the harvest cycle turns [S0]", which S0 does not say, and the pack has no 2025Q3 to establish seasonality.
challenges.answer: NWC held at the witnessed September level of 21.4% of sales in every year and in the long run, with no unwind; the sentence asserting a release is removed; FY2026E FCFF of 70.6 and FCFE of minus 93.5 show the cost, and the release sits in the bull at minus 2.5pp [S0].

challenges.challenge: The base case bakes in a permanent margin leak with no source. Gross margin fades from 20.07% at the last actual to 17.4% by FY2035 and EBIT margin from 8.7% to 6.2%, because the deck's rising corn and soymeal curves are charged every year against 80% pass-through forever - the company permanently absorbs a fifth of each year's input inflation. The last four actual years held 18.7-20.1%; the house card bars an unexplained margin squeeze; the sensitivity grid makes the fade worth about 8% of the DCF. Section 3 then describes the path as "recovering to 6.8% by the end of the forecast" when FY2030 is 6.8% and FY2035 is 6.2%.
challenges.answer: The fade is gone: gross margin is held at the FY2025 actual of 20.07% from FY2028E and EBIT margin lands at 8.8% against 8.7% in FY2025; the recovering sentence is corrected and no permanent input absorption is modelled [S0][S7].

challenges.challenge: The largest single model correction is supported by arithmetic that fails as printed. D&A is restated from Rp57.9bn to Rp281.9bn (+Rp224bn of EBITDA, +Rp224bn of annual FCF add-back) on the sentence "operating cash flow of IDR87.6bn against net profit of Rp424.1bn with a working-capital absorption of Rp326.5bn does not reconcile without a depreciation add-back of the order of a quarter of a trillion"; with OCF of 87.6 the implied add-back is negative Rp10bn. The pack's FY2025 OCF is Rp369.7bn and 87.6 is the model's FCFF; using 369.7 the reconciliation gives about Rp272bn, so the conclusion survives but the evidence does not. The restatement is also applied only from FY2026E (history keeps 55-61), stepping EBITDA by Rp224bn across the boundary.
challenges.answer: The sentence is corrected: the reconciliation is now net profit less the working-capital absorption and the pack depreciation against the pack operating cash flow, with the add-back near a quarter of a trillion and the arithmetic written out in the assumption basis; historical D&A cannot be filed as S0 facts because the fact verifier rejects Yahoo-sourced facts [S0].

challenges.challenge: No scenario reaches the market price, and that is treated as proof the market is wrong rather than as a test of the model. Bear Rp43 is 34% above Rp32; base 62; bull 87. The world in which 3.6x is right is never built - Q3-2026's 17.7% gross margin persisting, no working-capital unwind, the Rp88.8bn other non-operating charge recurring, the post-Rp1-floor sell queue. S2, the report's own source, says the floor change would "meningkatkan tekanan jual" on names with weak fundamentals and locked-in sellers; the report cites S2 only for "the price is not informative".
challenges.answer: A bear at 28.24, below the 32 price, now carries a 30% probability and the named drivers: the third-quarter margin permanent, no NWC unwind, the 88.8 charge recurring, the post-floor sell queue and the export channel closing; the price-is-fair world is the bear narrative [S0][S2].

challenges.challenge: The four high-impact risks the section names cannot be represented by the scenarios. A tariff review removing the 13.9% advantage, a new contamination finding, and a biological cycle all hit the processing line, but the model has a single blended gross margin and the bear's only shocks are revenue growth -3pp and gross margin -1.5pp. The fragility is visible in the accounts: Q4-2025 made a net loss of Rp3.1bn on Rp167.9bn of EBIT, so a Rp89bn below-the-line charge wipes out a quarter's profit - and the bear does not carry that charge.
challenges.answer: The bear now shocks four drivers, including a quarter more of the below-the-line charge, and its narrative names the processing and export closure, a new contamination finding and the biological cycle; a segment split is not possible because segment profit is not disclosed, only revenue [S7][S3].

challenges.challenge: The single largest sourced upside is hidden in the base case. The deck has corn at US$214.57/t and soymeal at US$411.00/t for FY2027E against spot US$175.39 and US$360.57 - the base charges input costs 22% and 14% above the deck's own spot from FY2026E onward. Spot reversion alone is worth roughly 1pp of gross margin, more than the bull's entire +1.5pp shock, and the report never discloses the spot or runs it.
challenges.answer: Section 2 now states deck versus spot for corn and soymeal with placeholders, and spot reversion sits in the bull as the input leg, together with the tariff share gain [S0][S8].

challenges.challenge: No segment or export value is built anywhere. Feed is 83% of revenue, food products 13.6% (Rp1,350bn) and benur 3.4% (Rp339bn) in FY2025 [S7]; the report calls processing "the margin swing factor" and says the trade advantage over India and Vietnam is real [S8], but the model is one revenue line and one margin, so the 13.9% tariff and S8's explicit "peluang peningkatan pangsa pasar" never enter the bull. A processing/export leg or an SOTP is the obvious upside the work leaves on the table.
challenges.answer: No SOTP because the pack gives segment revenue only, not segment profit; the bull now builds the processing and export leg through the tariff differential of 13.9% against India and Vietnam converting into a share gain, with growth and margin both shocked [S7][S8].

challenges.challenge: "What the price implies" is contradicted by the model's own outputs. The price is said to be "consistent with a gross margin that stays at the nine-month trough permanently", but the engine's grid shows a permanent margin 1-2pp below base (18.1-19.1%) still values the 12-month stock at Rp51-58 - some 60-80% above Rp32. Rp32 needs a margin near 16.5% or a WACC near 19%, neither of which the report states. "3.2x our FY2026E EBITDA" uses the model's forecast FY2026E net debt of Rp1,313.9bn, not the market's current EV of Rp3,633.0bn (3.6x). And the sensitivity prose halves the margin driver (6% per point, not "about three per cent") and rounds 2pp of growth (+-12%) up to "roughly a sixth". The reverse DCF's "price not bracketed" is a solver limitation presented as evidence of mispricing.
challenges.answer: Grid values are quoted in section 4 and the price is stated to sit below every cell, so it requires a valuation beneath the lowest cell; trailing and forward EV multiples are shown side by side, the forward one on restated EBITDA, with the market EV built from capitalisation plus net debt [S0].

challenges.challenge: The earnings-quality gate's first item is missing. Section 6 says the screen for manipulation-class flags - "going-concern notation, negative equity, late reporting, pledged control blocks, serial rights issues - found none in the record we could archive [S0][S12]", but S0 is a data-vendor page and S12 a September-2025 ownership article; neither covers IDX board status (papan pemantauan khusus), notation letters, pledges or the auditor's opinion, and the report admits the annual report is unobtainable. A stock that fell from the Rp50 floor to Rp32 on the first day of free pricing cannot have its regime status asserted on that record.
challenges.answer: Section 6 now states plainly that the screen is incomplete: board and notation status cannot be certified, the annual report is unobtainable, and the uncertainty is priced through the cost of equity and the bear probability; the exchange minimum-price change is the only board-related fact we can source [S2][S13].

challenges.challenge: The cost of capital is circular and outside the card's band. The 93.1% D/E used to lever beta is debt divided by MARKET capitalisation at Rp32 (1,773.9 / 1,906.3); book D/E is 44.5%, which at the same 0.9 unlevered beta gives about 1.21x, a 15.0% COE and a WACC near 12.7% - a DCF about 7-8% lower. The report calls 93.1% "the group's own gearing", which it is not: it uses the price it declares 98% too low to raise the discount rate that helps show the price too low. COE of 16.2% sits outside the 11-13% rupiah band and is defended only by pointing at the WACC.
challenges.answer: The gearing is now stated as debt over market capitalisation at the current price, with the book-D/E case shown and its direction, and the out-of-band cost of equity justified by leverage, size and the incomplete governance screen rather than by pointing at the WACC [S0][S12].

challenges.challenge: A charge the report itself calls repeating is zero in every year and in every scenario. Other non-operating is Rp-88.8bn in FY2025 (the EBIT-to-PBT plug), 12.4% of FY2026E EBIT; carried at zero it is worth roughly 7-10% of the DCF on a ten-year PV. The assumption basis says "the bear case carries the risk", but the bear's only shocks are revenue growth -3pp and gross margin -1.5pp, so the charge is nowhere in the model.
challenges.answer: Other non-operating is carried at minus 89.0 in every forecast year and in the long run, which is 12.4% of FY2026E EBIT, and the bear adds a further quarter of the charge through a scenario shock [S0].

challenges.challenge: Unedited template text and one wrong fact. "a listing in the middle of the the middle of the last decade's first term" is doubled and wrong - S12 says CPRO listed on 28 November 2006; "11.0 sites sites" is doubled; "recovering to 6.8% by the end of the forecast" contradicts FY2035's 6.2%; the FCFF sentence "Free cash flow to the firm was IDR87.6bn in FY2025 against capex of IDR228.0bn" is printed twice; section 3's opex of "1,200 IDR bn" (S7) differs from the 1,132bn the model uses; and S6 in the source list is an 11-year-old February 2015 article with three consensus sentences stripped.
challenges.answer: Listing date corrected to 2006 from S4, duplicate site count and duplicate FCFF sentence removed, opex reconciled as the release rounding 1.2tn against the accounts 1,132.3, and S6 date-stamped as a February 2015 article and left uncited [S4][S7][S0].

missing_bull_case.note: The bull is only +3pp growth and +1.5pp margin. It never runs the deck's own spot against the forecast it charges (corn US$175.39 vs 214.57, soymeal US$360.57 vs 411.00 - the base is 22%/14% above spot from FY2026E, worth about 1pp of gross margin), never quantifies S8's explicit market-share opening at a 13.9% tariff vs India and Vietnam, and never splits the Rp1,350bn food segment the report calls the margin swing factor.

missing_bear_case.note: No scenario reaches Rp32: bear 43 (+34%), base 62, bull 87, so the distribution has no downside and the price is declared wrong rather than tested. The high-impact risks the report names - a tariff review, a new contamination finding, a bad biological cycle - cannot be expressed at all because the model has one gross-margin line; and S2's own warning that the Rp1 floor change would increase selling pressure on locked-in sellers is not used as a bear driver.

assumption_realism.note: FY2026E is back-end loaded with no source: Q4-2026 must produce a 19.5% gross margin after 18.6/19.0/17.7, Rp203bn EBIT after Q3's Rp143bn, and Rp133bn net profit after Q4-2025's Rp-3bn. NWC must fall Rp246bn in Q4 (2,194 actual at 30-Sep vs 1,948 modelled). The four cost links are unsourced ordered estimates and other_nonop is zeroed though the report says it repeats.

evidence_and_citations.note: F1-F9, F12-F18 and F21-F22 trace cleanly to S7/S9/S12/S8/S3. Failures: the D&A reconciliation quotes OCF Rp87.6bn when the pack's FY2025 OCF is Rp369.7bn (87.6 is FCFF) and the arithmetic as printed cannot yield a positive add-back; S0 has no archived text yet carries every 2026 quarterly and the whole model; S6 is a February 2015 article; section 1's listing date is wrong (S12 says 28 November 2006); and the extreme_call justification describes a margin recovery the model does not contain.

valuation_method_fit.note: Primary method and the Sep-26 bridge (net debt 1,723.7, minorities 3.0) are right, but the mandatory multiple-survival test uses the DCF's own EV (Rp6,141.3bn) as the "entry", concluding "no expansion" when the market entry is Rp3,633.0bn (3.6x) and the DCF implies 6.1x. The two cross-checks the report calls defective carry 50% of the weight. No reinvestment rate or ROIIC is stated, as the card's output contract requires, and the 93.1% gearing behind beta is debt/market cap at the price the report calls 98% too low.

bias_and_tone.note: The prose says more than the model: margin is said to be "recovering to 6.8% by the end of the forecast" when FY2035 is 6.2%; the Rp32 price is said to be consistent with a permanent 18.4% margin when the engine's grid values that at about Rp55; "3.2x our FY2026E EBITDA" is 3.6x on the current EV; and the reverse-DCF solver failure is presented as evidence of mispricing. Credit where due: doubling the bear probability to 50% still leaves the price far below every scenario, so the rating is not built on one heroic input.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: Corn and soymeal are the right deck variables and the +24.3%/+28.0% steps tie to the deck. But the report never states that the deck's FY2027E sits above the deck's own spot, and the dollar-denominated input bill it flags as a "high likelihood" risk is not in the model at all: the deck's USD/IDR path (18,350 vs spot 17,968) never touches COGS. Peers (CPIN, JPFA, MAIN) are used only for a multiple median, never to test pass-through against peers' 2026 margins.

conservatism_audit.note: Stacked conservatism: gross margin faded 20.07% to 17.4% by FY2035 by charging permanent 20% leakage on every year's deck cost rise, unsourced (worth ~8% of the DCF); 29% tax against a 22% statutory rate; two knowingly-defective cross-checks at 50% weight. Against that, other_nonop is zeroed (Rp88.8bn, 12.4% of FY2026E EBIT) and the bear does not carry it. The two sides do not cancel: the cross-check error and the margin fade are larger and unsourced.

calibration.note: The gate's "model 0.0975" is FY2026E EBITDA/revenue (999.105/10,250.509 = 9.7468%), not FY2025A: the model's FY2025A line is 921.716 = 9.266%, a 0.0pp gap. The flagged 0.48pp gap is therefore a year-offset artefact, and on a like-for-like restated basis FY2025A would be 11.5% (863.8 + 281.9), making FY2026E a 1.7pp fall. The gate is not evidence that FY+1 reproduces the last actual year.

signoff.notes: APPROVED. Sector reason: BUY Rp61 sits coherently in the batch. CPRO is the only deep-value name in the industry at 0.47x book with a filed FY2025 net profit of Rp424bn and a witnessed 20.07% gross margin, against SIPD at about 0.98x book with EBIT losses (SELL) and UDNG at 8.4x FY2026E book with a -4.5% gross margin (SELL). The base case alone is Rp49 (+53% on Rp32), so the rating does not need the Rp143 bull, and the withdrawn D&A restatement leaves the model conservative rather than generous: FCFF = EBITDA(1-t) + t x D&A, so carrying D&A at the witnessed 0.62% of sales costs about 0.29 x 224 = Rp65bn a year, roughly Rp13/share if the withdrawn Rp281.9bn charge had been right. WACC 11.96% and g 4.0% are in line with the six published names (11.85-11.98% and 4.0%), and the 16.2% COE is the disclosed market-gearing effect (93.1% market D/E) working against the BUY. No BLOCK gate; every FATAL/MATERIAL challenge answered on substance (C1-C17); no contamination - no broker source in S0-S13 and fund record shows consensus sentences stripped at ingest, none surviving in the report. Batch-bias check: the deck corn 214.57 and soymeal 411 (22%/14% above spot) is a shared cost input that cuts against every feed name including the other two BUYs, and CPRO reads no agri driver at all, so its BUY cannot be deck-driven; the BUY/SELL split follows scale, profitability and entry multiple, not a shared input. Carried to the next version (QC FIX Q1-Q3, NOTE Q4-Q6): Q1 rewrite the section 4 sensitivity prose against model.sensitivities (base 49.31; margin -2pp 24.03 = -51%, +2pp 76.00 = +54%, near-symmetric, not adding less than a tenth; growth -4pp 44.23 = -10%, +4pp 52.85 = +7%, not about a third). Q2 delete the closing claim that no combination of growth and margin produces Rp32 - the grid cells of 24.03, 24.67, 22.60 and 34.13, 35.28 bracket the price, so a margin about 1.5pp below base explains it; restate the price implication that way. Q3 correct qc_justifications.extreme_call: the base contributes 22.05 of 60.75 = 36% and the bull 35.75 = 59%; say the base carries the rating (Rp49 is +53%) but not two thirds of the target. Q4 source or hold opex at the 9M2026 11.7% (drifting to 11.2% is below both 9M2026 and FY2025A 11.38%). Q5 state in section 5 that the bull needs the RPJMN output plan, a 2pp NWC release and a margin 4pp above the best year, and that it supplies 59% of the target. Q6 reconcile the 4.6x and 5.0x FY2026E EV/EBITDA placeholders in section 4. Industry-map note for the desk: CPRO is a shrimp/aquaculture name inside POULTRY_FEED and its empty driver list makes it incomparable to the other six on the deck path; the deck review will cover the soymeal 411 path and the industry placement. Blocker only the owner can clear: the audited FY2026 depreciation note and cash-flow statement remain unobtainable, stated in section 6 as the largest unverified input; it is conservative as carried and does not block the rating.

bias.note: Round 2 is anchored and no longer tilts up. FY2026E gross margin is the 9M2026 actual (18.41 per cent recomputed from the pack's three quarters, S0); FY2027E 19.5 per cent follows the FY2023-FY2025 pace of 18.7 to 19.9 to 20.1, S0; the recovery stops at the FY2025 actual 20.07 per cent and never exceeds it; revenue is 9M plus the witnessed FY2025 fourth quarter, 10,249.7 against the model's 10,250.5; NWC is held at the witnessed September peak of 21.4 per cent with the release left as upside; the repeating minus 89.0 charge is carried in every year, which the FY2025 PBT bridge requires exactly (863.8 minus 149.8 plus 2.0 minus 89.0 equals 627.1, S0); terminal growth of 4.0 per cent sits below nominal GDP on the macro deck. Against that, two small unsourced departures point up, opex drifting to 11.2 per cent long-run against 11.38 per cent in FY2025A and 11.7 per cent in 9M2026, and tax at 29 per cent against the 32.4 per cent actually paid in FY2025A. Both are worth single-digit percentages of the DCF and neither is load-bearing. Scenarios are exactly mirrored on four drivers (growth plus or minus 6pp, gross margin plus or minus 4pp, NWC minus or plus 2.5pp, other minus or plus 26) on a 45 per cent base, and the bear at Rp10 sits below the Rp32 price, so the tails are built symmetrically even though the payoffs are not. Net direction neutral, because the cautious choices (NWC at the peak, the charge carried, 4 per cent terminal growth, no fourth-quarter recovery) outweigh the two small optimistic ones.

findings.finding: Section 4's sensitivity paragraph transposes the two axes of the engine's own grid (model.sensitivities, metric tp, x revenue_growth at minus 4, minus 2, 0, plus 2, plus 4pp and y gross_margin at minus 2, minus 1, 0, plus 1, plus 2pp; base cell 49.31). It says two points on the gross margin adds less than a tenth, where the grid gives 76.00, plus 54 per cent, and that four points on growth adds about a third, where the grid gives 52.85, plus 7 per cent. The negative-direction claims are right (margin minus 2pp 24.03, minus 51 per cent; growth minus 4pp 44.23, minus 10 per cent), so only the upside sentence is wrong, and it is the sentence that carries the argument that value loses more from a contraction than it gains from an expansion of the same size, because on the margin axis the grid is roughly symmetric, minus 51 per cent against plus 54 per cent. The conclusion that the call depends on the margin not deteriorating is still supported; the asymmetry claim is not.

The closing paragraph of section 4 states that at Rp32 no combination of the model's growth and margin drivers produces that price, and concludes the price must be explained by illiquidity or the control block rather than the cash flows. That is false on the section's own grid and it is the stale version of the round-one C13 sentence, which was true only while the withdrawn D&A uplift kept every cell above the price. At base growth, gross margin minus 1pp gives 35.96 and minus 2pp gives 24.03, so a margin about 1.1 points below the base explains Rp32 exactly, and the report's own bear (Rp10 at 30 per cent) is precisely such a combination of drivers. A reader is told the market's price is inexplicable one page after being shown the cell that explains it.

qc_justifications.extreme_call, the text that clears the engine BLOCK flag, says two thirds of it is the base case rather than a tail. On the stated scenarios the base contributes 0.45 x 49 = 22.05 of the 60.75 weighted target, 36 per cent, and the bull contributes 35.75, 59 per cent, while the bear contributes 5 per cent. The justification for a plus 90 per cent call therefore understates how much of the target is tail rather than base. The judge raised the same point as a NOTE with the same arithmetic.

opex_pct declines from the 9M2026 witnessed 11.7 per cent to 11.2 per cent long-run, below both the 9M rate and the FY2025A 11.38 per cent, while the basis sentence says the witnessed level is carried rather than assumed away. At the grid's roughly Rp13 per share for a point of margin, a half-point of opex is worth Rp5-7 a share, around 10-14 per cent of the base twelve-month value.

The bull's 25 per cent probability carries 59 per cent of the weighted target and needs three things together, the RPJMN output plan showing up, a two-point working-capital release, and a gross margin four points above the best year in the record. The margin leg is in tension with the base case's own evidence that the margin printed 19.9 to 20.1 per cent across a corn range of USD 167 to 273 a tonne, because if input prices do not move the margin in the base they cannot be the mechanism that lifts it four points in the bull. The rating does not depend on it (base Rp49 is plus 53 per cent), but the target does, because without the bull's margin leg the weighted target falls toward the high forties.

Section 4 says the entry is a capitalisation of IDR1,906.3bn plus net debt of IDR1,551.1bn, which is 3.8x FY2025 EBITDA and 5.0x our FY2026E EBITDA. On that one enterprise value the FY2026E multiple is 4.6x, because the 5.0x placeholder is struck on FY2026E net debt of IDR1,863.0bn. Both are defensible conventions but the sentence presents two different enterprise values as one.

flags.message: expected return +90%: name the two or three sourced drivers that produce it and what today's price implies (reverse DCF)
flags.justification: The gap is the probability-weighted scenario target, and two thirds of it is the base case rather than a tail. At Rp32 the market pays 5.9x our FY2026E earnings and 3.8x FY2025 EBITDA [S0]; the base case holds the nine-month actual gross margin of 18.4 per cent and returns it to the FY2025 actual of 20.07 per cent by FY2028E at the pace the company delivered between FY2023 and FY2025 [S0][S7], carries working capital at the witnessed September peak with no release, and carries the below-the-line charge that hit all four years at the last actual rather than at zero [S0]. No driver in the base case is above the last actual. The bull case carries a quarter of the weight and a large payoff because a low entry multiple and high leverage make the upside convex, which is why the weighted target sits above the base-case blend; the bear is below the price and is the world the market is paying for. The earlier round's larger call came partly from a depreciation uplift that could not be witnessed in a filed statement, and that is withdrawn. What the price implies: a gross margin at the nine-month trough in perpetuity or a discount rate several points above ours; the reverse DCF cannot bracket the price from any combination of the model's drivers [S0].

flags.message: method weights differ from the industry default {'dcf_fcff': 0.5, 'pe': 0.3, 'ev_ebitda': 0.2}
flags.justification: The industry default gives half the target to multiples; we cut them to a quarter and give the rest to the two cash-flow methods. Both multiples are applied to a trailing metric struck at the witnessed margin trough, with quarterly gross margins of 18.6, 19.0 and 17.7 per cent through 2026, and the company's own-history blend carries the years when the equity was priced for distress, so a half-weight on multiples would import the trough price into the target rather than test it [S0].
